chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Yūnus al-Shaybānī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, “May I give the adhan while I am riding?” He said, “Yes.” I said, “Then may I give the iqamah while I am riding?” He said, “No.” I said, “And may I give the iqamah while my foot is in the stirrup?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then may I give the iqamah while I am sitting?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then may I give the iqamah while I am walking?” He said, “Yes, walking toward the salat (prayer).” He then said, “When you give the iqamah for the salat (prayer), then give it in a measured manner, for indeed you are in the salat (prayer).” He said: I said, “I had asked you whether I may give the iqamah while I am walking, and you said yes; so is it permissible for me to walk in the salat (prayer)?” He said, “Yes, when you enter from the door of the masjid and say the takbir while you are with a just Imam, then walk toward the salat (prayer), that suffices for you. And if the Imam has said the takbir for rukuʿ, you have been with him in that rakʿah, because if you catch him while he is bowing, but you have not caught the takbir, then you have not been with him in the rukuʿ.”

key_terms.أُؤَذِّنُ: I give the adhan, the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)
key_terms.أُقِيمُ: I give the iqamah, the commencement call immediately before salat (prayer)
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ: a just Imam leading the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ: a rakʿah, one unit of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer), including the congregational prayer context here
key_terms.لِلرُّكُوعِ: for rukuʿ, the bowing position in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a person give the iqamah while walking or riding, and how does one join the Imam in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings related to the adhan and iqamah, distinguishing between what may be done while riding, sitting, or walking. It also clarifies a practical ruling about joining congregational salat (prayer), especially when entering the masjid and catching the Imam before rukuʿ.
